# adr-system

<!-- awf:edit current-state: from .awf/domains/parts/adr-system/current-state.md -->
## Current state

ADRs are append-only history, not active authority: active rules and invariants live as current-state topic claims. Each numbered ADR routes by its authored format marker, independent of its number: marker absence selects the frozen legacy parser, while `current-state-v1`, `current-state-v2`, `current-state-v3`, and `current-state-v4` select their matching governed parser. A numberless record is valid only in the running binary's current authoring format, which is how a pending record joins the corpus before it is numbered. Every governed format uses the ordered Context, Decision, State changes, Consequences, Alternatives Considered, and Status history sections, V3 is V2 plus a mandatory retained `slug:` key and the pending identity form. V4 retains exact Decision item blocks and adds unique stable `decision:` slugs; these are navigation identity, never active authority or currentness inference. The activation registry owns the current authoring marker used by scaffolding; adding a future format adds its parser, transition matrix, activation generation, and older-format compatibility proofs rather than a number cutoff. Decisions live under `docs/decisions/`, parsed by `internal/adr` and rendered into the generated drift-checked `INDEX.md`. Ordinary commits may introduce only the registry's current format. A real merge may import an exact older-format record carried by an incoming parent when the final trailer block carries its adjacent version-and-reason authorization pair; the merge may apply only sanctioned numbering or renumbering substitutions, never a format retrofit or semantic edit.

V2, V3, and V4 statuses are Proposed, Accepted, Implementing, Implemented, and Abandoned. Their history is a date-nondecreasing prefix-append-only event stream. Status events repeat the latest content stamp, and Amended events record each post-Accepted amendment. Applied events use the exact grammar `- <date>: Applied; operations: <declaration-ordered operation-list>`. Entering Implementing appends status then a first nonempty strict-subset batch, a middle pair appends one batch, and the final pair appends the remainder then Implemented. Direct terminal transitions use one implicit batch. While another operation remains, a Reapplied event may correct an already-applied add or update in one material transaction without changing declaration progress or first-application provenance; removes, events before Applied, and corrections after the final batch are refused. Abandonment preserves applied operations, cancels the remainder, and carries a rationale. Outside the bounded Reapplied route, stable history is corrected forward through a successor ADR.

The `## State changes` section is the authoritative relationship between an ADR and the topics it governs: either `None.` or a list of `- add`, `- update`, and `- remove` entries, each naming one claim by its qualified `<domain>/<topic>:<slug>` id. awf derives the affected topics and domains from these operations, so a v1 ADR carries no `topics`, `related`, `tags`, or `domains` frontmatter; a rename is a remove plus an add, a split is one remove plus several adds, and a removed id is never reused. For every newly appended implicit or explicit application batch, `awf check staged` compares HEAD with the index and verifies exactly that transaction: an `add` claim appears with the ADR as `Origin`, an `update` preserves the claim's `Origin`, unions its `Revised-by` with the updating ADR at its ascending position, and changes a canonical field, and a `remove` leaves no active claim. An applied remove is an absorbing tombstone: a later update of the removed id is retained as dominated history with no current effect and an empty required mutation set, and absence stays attributed to the remove. Static `awf check` validates the lifecycle, operation history, claim provenance, digest, and absence rules; the first v1 update or remove for an identity sealed into the migration baseline is allowed to begin without a v1 add operation, while every claim absent from that frozen baseline begins with exactly one add. `awf audit` and implementation review evaluate every parent-to-commit snapshot pair in an explicit range rather than only its endpoints.

Append-only protects rationale, not orthography (ADR-0115, widened by ADR-0118): once frozen, an ADR's arguments, decision items, alternatives, and consequences are never rewritten, but a meaning-preserving punctuation normalization of its authored body is permitted, proven word-preserving by an alphanumeric-run comparison that must report zero delta. A V2 body's meaning stays amendable until a terminal status with each amendment recorded as an Amended event, a V1 body freezes once it leaves Proposed, and a meaning-preserving schema retrofit may migrate either encoding, the license under which the project-atomic upgrade rewrote the legacy corpus into the v1 format.

`INDEX.md` always renders, with placeholder sections when no ADR is in flight or recorded, so its document-map link resolves out of the box (ADR-0020). It lists Proposed, Accepted, and Implementing ADRs under an In flight section and Implemented and Abandoned ADRs under a compact History by number, title, and status, and renders no supersession chains, anchor annotations, currentness inference, or per-domain ADR index; generated domain docs link a compact topic list instead. A new ADR is scaffolded via `awf new adr "<title>"` (ADR-0042), which copies `template.md` with its marker comments stripped and its date and title filled in; `awf-proposing-adr` invokes it as the first authoring step. What identity it gets depends on the branch (ADR-0202): on the configured `integrationBranch` it takes the next sequential number as `NNNN-<slug>.md`, and anywhere else it is pending, written as `<slug>.md` with an `# ADR-<slug>:` heading. A pending record is a full corpus member, implementable to completion in a worktree, and is blocked from reaching the integration branch unnumbered. `awf adr number [<slug>...]` assigns the numbers at integration, after merging the integration branch in and before merging back: it renames the file, rewrites the heading, substitutes `ADR-<slug>` in authored `Origin:` and `Revised-by:` lines, re-renders, and prints the `<slug> -> NNNN` mapping for the integration commit message. The retained `slug:` key survives numbering, so a reference written while the record was pending stays resolvable. A number once assigned never changes; a numbering that raced another integration is unmade by reset and remade, never renumbered. The ADR guide (`README.md`), the skeleton (`template.md`), and a plan-authoring guide (`plans/README.md`) are awf-managed singletons (ADR-0021, ADR-0020), so the `.layout.adrReadme` / `.layout.adrTemplate` / `.layout.plansReadme` references resolve in any adopter project. The workflow chain (brainstorm → ADR → plan → resync → impl → review) is enforced by the `awf-*` skills and reviewer agents.
